what: Wintrust is a Chicago-area bank holding company that runs fifteen separately branded community banks, plus a large insurance premium finance business and a mortgage operation.
customers: Households and small businesses around Chicago and Milwaukee, and insurance brokers nationally through premium finance.
money: the spread on loans funded by deposits
trust, brokerage and home lending fees
moat: Separately branded local banks that feel like community institutions while sharing one balance sheet and technology, which has won deposits from larger rivals for decades.
risks: Commercial real estate in the Chicago area is a meaningful exposure
Deposit competition raises funding costs quickly when rates rise
Mortgage banking revenue swings with rates
opportunities: 11.3 times earnings with a 30.2% net margin and $1.7B of free cash flow
Revenue grew from $1.7B to $2.7B in four years
Analysts see about 19% upside, with 16 covering the stock
watch: Net interest margin and credit quality in commercial real estate.
